meta.title: An Edge-Cloud Collaborative Framework for Latency Optimization in Prompt Injection Defense

problem.v: Cloud-side rechecking of suspicious prompts creates queueing and p99 latency spikes
problem.q: cloud-side checking itself can become a queueing bottleneck

main_idea.v: Edge detector splits requests into low/medium/high risk; Q-TRiG queue-aware policy decides cloud recheck vs restricted mode for medium risk
main_idea.q: enlarges the stable operating region under heavy load

threat_model.v: Input-side prompt injection against LLM services in edge-cloud deployments

models_tested.name: MiniLM embeddings + Random Forest (edge); OpenAI embeddings + RF; DeBERTa (cloud recheck)

metrics.name: Cloud queueing delay, p99 end-to-end latency, offloading ratio

results.claim: Edge detector accuracy RF: MiniLM 0.9533, OpenAI embeddings 0.9723
Risk split MiniLM: low 56.69%, mid 30.49%, high 12.82%
Q-TRiG keeps cloud waiting and p99 low across load 5-45 req/s while COR, EBG, S-TRiG diverge (shown in figures; no numeric speedups in text)

limitations_inferred: [INFERENCE] Simulation only; no real LLM, attack traffic or security-effectiveness measurement

reusable_for_our_project.v: Idea: route medium-risk requests to a restricted execution mode (no tools, limited context, safe template)
reusable_for_our_project.q: disabling tool use, restricting context sources, or returning a safe template

flags: Main results are in figures; extract numbers manually if cited
Low direct relevance to attack evaluation; moderate for defense design
